utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in this courtroom; and also those who can watch us through videolink, good morning, Mr. Doraiswamy, in Zagreb. Before we start with the examination of the witness, I'd first like to inform the parties that the Chamber has decided to the grant the protective measures as requested; reasons to follow. That means face distortion and pseudonym for Witness 69. I would also like to inform the parties that the Chamber has decided, being advised to do so by The Victims and Witness Section, to have short sessions, in view of the medical condition and the age of Witness 69. That means sessions of approximately one hour, and have breaks which are a little bit longer than usual. Further, the parties are informed that Witness 69 has some hearing problems, although it has been tested, and it seems that he does understand. He can hear. What he needs to hear, especially with the earphones on, it is acceptable. But for you to be aware, if there is any mal-communication, that it might be due to this hearing problem. Then, finally, I'm also informed that the witness who has not a perfect sight, which is not surprising at this age, has also forgotten bring his glasses, which might cause some additional problems, but we'll see how to overcome them. Finally, on the basis of the conversations the witness has had with The Victims and Witness Section, it appears that he is fully capable of understanding and communicating with others, if you don't mix up too many matters at the same time. Even at my age, I'm already sometimes confused by composite questions, et cetera. So let's try to keep matters so simple that the witness understands them and that the Chamber understands them as well. Mr. Tieger, who is going to examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you. Mr. Hedaraly will takes this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hedaraly, are you ready to call your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, yes, Mr. Doraiswamy, would you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The Prosecution would like to call Witness 69.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we do so, we have to fix some problems with the earphones, but that is a matter of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Has it been fixed? Then, Mr. Doraiswamy, could you please take care that the witness enters the room in which you are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 69. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can hear you well. I can hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we start, I would like to ask you, Mr. Registrar, to inform the Chamber about who is present in the room you are in at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you, Your Honour, and good morning to everybody in the courtroom. Beside me is the witness, and I also have the audio/visual technician. There are three of us present in the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that information. Witness 69 before you give evidence, the Rules require you to make a solemn declaration. The solemn declaration is that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text has been handed out to you. I hope you can read it. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness 69, the Chamber has decided that the protective measures you are asked for, that is, face distortion and pseudonym, are granted. That means that we are not using your own name. We will just call you Witness 69. The parties are hereby urged to take care that not, by questions, for the clue to the identity of the witness could be given, so to ask for private session whenever needed. You will first be examined by Mr. Hedaraly, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Hedaraly, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. Registrar in Zagreb. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I could first have 65 ter number 4860, which is tab 1, for Mr. Registrar in Zagreb; and that's a pseudonym sheet, so if we could not publish that outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Witness, can you please confirm that these are your personal details?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Registrar, if we could pull up 65 ter number 4858 on the screen, under seal, again. This is tab 2 for Mr. Registrar in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall being interviewed by representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor on 31 May 1997 and providing a written statement on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did you have a chance to review that statement yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I understand that there are some corrections that needs -- that need to be made regarding the bodies that you discovered in your hamlet: Which ones you observed yourself and of which ones you were told by someone else. Would you like to make that clarification now for the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please invite the witness, again, if he talks about bodies, to be clear that he talks about brothers and sisters, or whatever, but not specific persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If you could just refer to the first names of the bodies that you saw and not mention the family names?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The names are common enough, Your Honour, that that should guard confidentiality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I can help you. How many bodies did you yourself see in your hamlet when you returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: I saw only one in my courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what was the name, and only the first name, of the person that you found in your courtyard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Ilija.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the other four bodies mentioned in your statement, you were told about these bodies by someone else. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: A woman who is not quite sane told me. She was walking about freely. She was allowed to move around freely. She told me about that, but I didn't see it myself because I didn't normally use that road, that path.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. If you can look back at your witness statement in front of you, is that your signature at the bottom left of the first page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So does that signature mean that, subject to the correction that we just made about the bodies, it accurately reflects what you told to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the contents of that statement that you signed in May 1997 were true to the best of your knowledge and recollection at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And, finally, if you were asked the same questions today that you were asked in 1997, you would give the same answers to the extent that you could remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, I have forgotten a lot of things. I'm getting on in age, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I understand that. But to the extent that you could remember, you said that this statement was accurate. So you would, to the extent that your memory would allow you, give the same answers to those questions today, would you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes and no. I simply cannot remember all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: But you did sign that statement in 1997, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes. But I had a stroke in the meantime, and the disease does its dirty work.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: But to the extent that you signed this in 1997, you signed it because it was accurate, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Correct. Correct. That is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So if you were asked the same questions today, if you remember these answers, they would be the same as the ones that you gave in that statement that you signed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, certainly, except that today I wouldn't have been able to remember all of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that this comes as close to as an attestation under 92 bis as possible and that, of course, Rule 92 bis does not pay attention to time as a factor which might disable a witness to give exactly the same answers, because he might have forgotten something about that. But as far as matters stand, unless I hear now from the Defence, this amounts to what 92 bis says, which, of course, leaves it open to say that to the extent the witness has lost recollection of certain matters, that it might have an impact on further questions to be put to him. The Chamber, of course, then will decide how to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the Gotovina Defence, we will would agree that -- I believe that Your Honour said "92 bis," I believe you mean "92 ter," if I am not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 92 ter, yes, because otherwise there would be no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With the caveat, however, I think this is what Your Honour was saying, to the extent that the inability to recollect impedes the cross-examination or our ability to inquire as to the matters in the statement, I would reserve on that point. But, yes, for purposes of the requirements of 92 ter, we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the question would arise whether 92 ter or, to some extent, 92 quater would come into play, although not literally applicable. Any other positions from the other Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Then, Mr. President, at this time, I would like to have 65 ter 4858 admitted into evidence, under seal, pursuant to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes:

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And we have a redacted version for Mr. Registrar that can be assigned a different number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try to take things in the proper order. First, pseudonym sheet, which is usually unobjected. Mr. Registrar, the pseudonym sheet would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P178, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P178 is admitted, under seal. Mr. Hedaraly then we have the 92 ter statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P179, Your Honours, also under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Then P179 is admitted, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: My apologies to the Bench and to Mr. Registrar for the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is easily accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 4859 on the screen also under seal for now. That's tab 3, Mr. Registrar in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Witness, do you also recall providing a second witness statement to representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor on 18 October 2004?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: 2004, I don't recall who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe it was an investigator that came to your hamlet, to your house, to ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: The investigator. I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, a female investigator with dark hair.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you take a look at the bottom right of that statement, of the English version of the statement that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, did you have a chance to review that statement yesterday? Was that statement read out to you by someone who spoke your language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, it was read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, that signature, does it mean that it accurately reflected what happened you said on that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And then the contents of that statement that you signed in 2004 were true to the best of your knowledge and recollection at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, referring back to the answers of the witness previously, I would like to move for admission under 92 ter at this moment without asking whether the answers would be the same today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, I take it, with the same pro vico with the previous 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Yes. Then, Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P180, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P180 is admitted into evidence, under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time, I would like to read a short summary of the evidence contained in those two witness statements; and if you inform the witness for the purpose of this, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will do so. Witness 69, since you have given statements already and since further questions may be put to you in relation to those statements, the Prosecutor now will read a summary of what is in those statements. You don't have to respond to it, just listen. It is mainly to inform the public about what is in your statement; and after that, further questions will be put to you. So just listen for the time being. Mr. Hedaraly, Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I believe a copy was provided to the interpretation booth. Witness 69 lived in a hamlet north of Knin when Operation Storm started in August 1995. On the 5th of August, at around 10.00 in the morning, his village was heavily shelled for about half an hour from the direction of Grahovo. His stable was hit and its roof was damaged . Later that day, Croatian soldiers, with a Croatian armoured vehicle, entered his village. One of these soldiers, in military uniform, forced his neighbour, Dmitar, who was 81 years old at the time, to go with him behind his house. He heard a burst of automatic gun-fire; and a week or so later, this elderly neighbour's body was found. Witness 69 escaped and fled to the woods, and he advised two friends who had sought refuge at his house, Milka and Ilija, who were and son, to do the same. From his hiding point, he saw Croatian soldiers lighting the house of one of his other neighbours, Djuka, on fire. He returned that night, under the cover of darkness, to find the body of Ilija, the son who had sought refuge with him, lying in his yard. He also met with other villagers hiding in the forest; and a day or two later, one of them noticed that her house had been burned. This woman confronted the Croatian soldiers and identified them to the witness as members of the Split Brigade. When he returned to his house on one occasion, a week or so later after the beginning of the operation, on the 11th or 12th August, he was told that the following bodies were discovered in addition to the body of Ilija, which was still lying there. These were the bodies of Dmitar, the 81-year-old man he saw being taken behind his house by a Croatian soldier; Milka, the mother of Ilija who had sought refuge in his house; Djuro; and one body that was not identified. In addition, he noticed on that day that his house had been ransacked; and in the course of the following days, while hiding in the woods, he observed Croatian soldiers in uniform looting the houses in his hamlet and taking valuable items away. His own valuable items were loaded onto his own tractor and taken away. Finally, Witness 69 made his way to the UN compound and left on the buses to Serbia with the other refugees on 17 September 1995. This concludes my summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm looking at Mr. President to see whenever a break is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll inform the witness. Witness 69, some questions will now be put to you. Whenever you think you need a break because you are tired, please tell us. I have in mind at this moment to allow Mr. Hedaraly to start with another 25 minutes of questioning, and then we will have a break. But if you feel not comfortable, if you get too much tired, please tell me, then we'll have a break a bit earlier. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can we just move into private session for a few questions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now without naming any of them, how many hamlets were there in your village?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. In your hamlet, how many houses were there in your specific hamlet, and please don't name it or don't name any of the inhabitants, but just the number of houses in your hamlet in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, there were about 20 houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And how many --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And how many -- how many people lived in your hamlet in August 1995 before Operation Storm began?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, quite a few of them, but it was impossible to count them all. And in the end, there were none. At one time, there were more people living in a single house than there are living in the whole hamlet now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: How many people are living in the hamlet now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, as I have told you, seven or eight people, women, all of them old.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And before, on average, in August 1995, in the 20 houses, on average, how many people would live in each house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, on the average, 50 or 60 of those members.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Sorry. Are you talking about 50 or 60 total in the house? I asked you - and maybe my question was unclear - how many people, on average, would live in each individual house of the 20 houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Oh, okay then. Five, six, seven, eight people per house; sometimes three, maybe two.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: No. There was not a single house where only two people lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that answer. I want to move now in your statement when you talk about your village being shelled on the 5th of August. I want to start with your hamlets which -- with your specific hamlet, and once again don't say the name. Can you please tell the Court how many shells fell in your hamlet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: That's what I can't recall. One hit my cousin's house and the other one hit my barn. I don't know how many shells hit our area, but I can tell that you the lower part of the village that is on the other side of the railway track that's where most of the shells fell. This was a more convenient target for them to shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me just focus on your hamlet. You said that there were at least - if I understood correctly - at least two shells fell in your hamlet specifically. Have I understood that correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can have 65 ter number 4884. Mr. Registrar in Zagreb, that is, I believe, the fourth picture behind tab 8. I don't know, Mr. Registrar, if there is a way to check that it is the same picture that we have on the screen here, whether Mr. Registrar there can make that -- sure. If Mr. Registrar in Zagreb could just show the picture to the camera, so we can confirm we have the same picture here on our screen. No. That's not the one. I think it's the one after that. No. Can you try the next one? I apologise for this. Okay. Can you go before then, please. No. The one before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we give some guidance, Mr. Registrar. It should be --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's the one. Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, Witness, on this picture, the building that we see partly covered in the trees on the left in white, is that your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And that building on the right, is that the barn that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The barn, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, have you asked the registry not to show this picture on the screen? We're in open session, and, of course, if no instructions are given that the picture should not be shown. I don't know whether there were or not. It may not have been shown, but you should be -- they have not been shown, but it's inadvertent if you never give instructions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we can go to the next picture, which was 65 ter 4883. I believe, Mr. Registrar in Zagreb, that will be the picture before. If we could not show that one to the public as well. No. It would be under tab 8. It's the one of his barn. It's a close-up of the right side of the previous picture. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, can you indicate for the Court where -- where the shell hit on this -- on this barn or house, and describe what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: It was hit here. Here, right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you circled in red, I'm assuming not at the tree, but at the spot on the roof behind the tree. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, that precisely was it. That's where the tree is on this picture, but it's in the same direction. I can't do it in any other way. Well, let's say here, here. Let me mark it this way then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have this exhibit entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What about the earlier pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That was simply for the demonstrative purposes, but we can admit it as well, if there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm not insisting on it, but I'm just inquiring into --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It would be helpful to have both of them, Your Honour, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, then, the first picture?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first picture with 65 ter 04884, that becomes Exhibit P181.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P181 is admitted into evidence. Then, the next one, the picture marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that was 65 ter number 04883 marked by the witness becomes Exhibit P182.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections from what I see. P182 is admitted into evidence; both P181 and P182, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, Witness, looking at this picture again, can you -- can you situate for the Court where that second shell that you said hit fell with respect to this -- to this picture of your barn. Was it behind it? Was it the right of it, to the left of it, in front of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: To the right, here. If you look at this area from this direction, here. Well, but -- here. That would be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So to the right side of what we see on the picture right now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. I'm not sure what we're -- which we're talking about now. I'm reading the witness' prior testimony where he says he recalls two shells, one that hit his barn and one that his cousins house. So I'm not sure, when Mr. Hedaraly phrased question, saying where the second shell hit, what shell we're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although, the cousin's house I think in the written statement was located somewhere as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It was unclear from the statement, Your Honour, so I want to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, please, could you put a more specific question to the witness in this respect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Go ahead. Witness, is there something that you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, no, actually I don't have anything to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So that second shell that you were talking about now that is not on the picture, is that the one that fell on your cousin's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. So that house and that yard where that second shell fell is located somewhere to the right of this picture you have in front of you, P182. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to object as to the leading here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean he already testified, and I'm trying to clarify. He said that it hit his house, he said it was on the right. I am just putting the two together, so that the record is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, his prior answer is: "Yes, in the yard," and then the follow up question is: "So it hit the house." That is not clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'll remove the house part and just use the yard. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Try to now, without adding anything, to see whether the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So the yard of your cousin's house where that second shell fell is located somewhere to the right of this picture you have in front of you, P182. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, let's take it step by step. When you said the second shell fell into the yard, the yard of what exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My cousin's yard, here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I saw you were pointing at the right side of the picture. Did you intend to say that your cousin's house was to the right of what we see in this picture, and that your cousin's house cannot be seen on the picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you can't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But is it to the right of your house on this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you stand here, in front of the yard, it's to the right, and the father's house is to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just for the record, the witness pointed to the right side of the picture, and then made a movement right up from there when he said where his cousin's house was. Please proceed Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now in your statement, you said that your village, not your hamlet but your village - and, once again, don't say the names of any areas in your village - you said that your village was shelled heavily. Now, did you see shells or did you hear shells? What's the basis of your knowledge that your village was shelled heavily?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'll phrase the question, Your Honour, I'm sorry. That was a bad question on my part. I saw Mr. Kehoe thought the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that your village was heavily shelled. What was the basis for that assertion you made in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, it was shelled, but one couldn't really count the shells. One could only run right down into the basement to take shelter. It was shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Could you hear the shells fall?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: We didn't hear the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, of course, yes, I did hear. It was like thunder. It was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And were there any ARSK soldiers in your hamlet, or in your village, the day of that shelling, the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: No. Well, that was after the shelling. That's when the troops came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, I am in fear that this is an misunderstanding in you using the abbreviation "ARSK" soldiers. Could you be more explicit?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I notice, too, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers of the Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina in your hamlet or in your village on the day of the shelling, the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: No, there were none. They had gone. They had fled.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers of the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina in your hamlet, or in your village, in the days preceding the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course. Before, there used to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: How long before are we talking about? I want you to focus on the week before the shelling, not years before, not months before, just the days before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, a week before, three or four days before. But they were already making plans where they should flee, what route that they should take as they fled. It was worse than the partizans.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And this was something that happened three or four days before the shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Three or four days before, that is when they were making the preparations. They were pulling out heavy weapons already. Well, I don't know who would recall all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that would be a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 69, we now have a break. After a break of approximately a little bit over half an hour, we'll resume. Is that okay, as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Then we will have a break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is convenient. But please not let us take this too late. We want to get home as soon as possible, don't we.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break of 35 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. That's what I like to hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Witness, I want now to direct your attention to when you went to hide in the woods the first time on the 5th of August. In your statement, you stated that before going into the woods, you removed some family items. Can you tell the Court what it is that you removed or that you hid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Only two, only two; no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Only two what, did you remove?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you two pistols.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did these pistols belong to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Not so much to me as to my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And where was your son at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: He wasn't there at the time. He had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when had he been killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: In June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. And then later on in your statement, you said that when you were hiding in the woods, you saw Croatian soldiers lighting the house of Djuka on fire. Can you please describe for the Chamber what it is that you saw?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to have to object again. I don't think that's what it says in the statement. It says in the statement: "I did not see the actual setting of fire."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So I would object to the mischaracterisation of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly will rephrase his question and perhaps read to you what was said in the statement and then ask for further explanation. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Maybe my using of "set ablaze" and "light" is different, but I will rephrase the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you read, then we have no --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Sure. "I saw that her house suddenly went up in flames, together with hayloft, so I assumed that the Croatian soldiers poured some gasoline on it. I did not see the actual setting of fire. I saw a group of Croatian soldiers but I could not specify their number." Then you say: "I knew they were Croatian soldiers because there was no other military presence in the area at that time." Now can you provide some clarification as to what you actually saw when the house went on fire, and please do not mention the name of the -- the last name of the person whose house was on fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes. I saw, perhaps 600 metres away, I saw that it was on fire. It was torched. They passed by a another house, not this one. It was about 60 [as interpreted] metres away from me. They went there and torched it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 4887, under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I again apologise for interrupting, but there is some confusion in the answer, whether it is 600 or 60 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard 600, but could you please verify with the witness, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness, but can you just clarify for us what distance was the house that you saw burning? Was it 60 metres or 600 metres?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go back to 65 ter 4887. That, I believe, Mr. Registrar in Zagreb, is the last picture behind tab 8, having an ERN of 0543-3877.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now I want -- Witness, I want to focus on the night of the 5th when you came back and that you saw the dead body of Ilija. So, first of all, I want to ask you on that picture that is in front of you, is that your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, that's my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, can you tell from this picture where you saw the body of Ilija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: I can. Outside the veranda which you cannot see from the vine branch --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. So what you're saying --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: -- towards the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you cannot see from this picture where the body is because you can only see the outside of the courtyard on this picture. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Correct, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Please, Your Honour, can I have this admitted in into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P183, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P183, under seal, is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if we can pull up 65 ter 4890, and that one has to be under seal, as well, because the name of the witness is on it. Mr. Registrar in Zagreb, this is the drawing that was provided to you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, Witness, at the bottom of this picture, there is sort of a door at the bottom centre of the sketch. Is that the gate that we saw on the previous picture that is it in red?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I must apologise, Your Honour, but I don't recall seeing this, and it says it was done on the 12th of May. I'm advised by my case manager that we didn't get a copy of this either, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It was e-mailed to counsel yesterday afternoon or last night, to all counsel. It came out of the proofing session yesterday, so I disclosed it to them right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will check my e-mail, Your Honour. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm pretty sure it's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed at this moment. But, of course, what the consequences are if there would not have been any disclosure is still to be seen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The e-mail was sent at 6.22 p.m. last night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I was not available at that time, and I don't know that our case manager was copied on it. But we can proceed, Your Honour, and we'll deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Witness, can you confirm for us that the at bottom at what looks like a door in the sketch at the bottom of the sketch is that -- the gate that we was saw on the previous picture that was in red?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the place where you saw Ilija is what is marked there in black with the line that says "Ilija," this is where you saw his body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So just so that we understand correctly, the body was found inside your courtyard that we saw in the previous picture. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Witness. I have only one last series of questions for you, and it is regarding the looting that you saw the Croatian soldiers perform over the days following Operation Storm. Now, when you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, you asked the witness questions about the sketch. What would you like to do with the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I would like to admit it into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see no objection from any of the Defence teams. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P184, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P184, under seal, is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement, you talked about Croatian soldiers coming and looting later on in your hamlet. Now, did you -- was it always the same soldiers coming and looting or were they different soldiers on different days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: There were different; they were not all the same. They came from Split, Zadar, all of them neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you recognise some of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: I recognised them when I came closer and saw them, but then what?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Where did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: They --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness be asked to repeat the last bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last portion of what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: I recognised these people, neighbours who lived in Zadar and Split. They were -- when the man of the house is not there, they do their business.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I just want to clarify. So some of these soldiers that came used to be your neighbours. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Neighbours, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were all of them former neighbours of yours, or were there some that you did not recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Of course, there were some who were not. One of them was leading the others to show them what is located where.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And were they all wearing Croatian army uniforms, as far as you could tell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: They were a mixed group. Some were; some were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: What about the specific incident that you mention in your statement, about the four soldiers that looted the house of your best man, first name Djoko, did you recognise those four soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: I did not. I did not dare come that close. I did not recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what about the ones that looted your own house, when you saw them take things on your tractor, did you recognise those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: I did not. I did not. I have to tell the truth. I did not dare come close.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's all have I for the Prosecution, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hedaraly. Witness 69, now Defence counsel will have an opportunity to put questions to you, and the first is Mr. Misetic, who is Defence counsel for Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 69.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 69.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the -- to your witness statement of 1997; and in your witness statement, you confirmed that your village was not exposed to shelling on the 4th of August, 1995, which was the first day of Operation Storm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: On the first day, there were operations -- I mean, on the second day, the army had left already; and the next morning, the shelling already started.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. But on the first day, there was no shelling in your village and hamlet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Not the first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But, in your statement, you say that your family and your fellow villagers left on that first day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court why your family and your fellow villagers left on the first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, I looked at what the others were doing, and I took up and left. Even sheep follow others to find better pastures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So you're saying that your fellow villagers left because other people were leaving the area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, on the 5th of August, which is the second day, Milica and Ilija appeared in your hamlet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Ilija was around 40 years old. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was Ilija a soldier of the Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: He had never been in the army, he never joined any operations, and he has a bad eye.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When Milica and Ilija arrived at your house, did they have any personal belongings with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: That's something I don't know. They had a satchel. Only we had a snack, a drink when the shelling started, and then we ran into the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that when you withdrew to the forest, you took two pistols with you. Do you know if Ilija --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. That mischaracterises the -- he said that he hid two pistols, not that he took them with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, you have to take them if you want to hide them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: But he is suggesting that he took them to the woods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is a suggestion which --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That was my understanding, but I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you please clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness, when you testified earlier about hiding two pistols, where did you hide the pistols?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: I threw them into the smoking house. That is it where the meat is cured, and that's where they remained. I just threw them in there and fled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you know if Ilija had any weapons when he arrived at your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: No. He didn't have anything. He was unarmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that: "Milka and Ilija stepped out from the civilian reclusive convoy and came to seek the refuge at my place." What civilian reclusive convoy are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, the whole column, they were heading back. They wanted to go back home because they figured out that was the only thing they could do, go back home. That's where they -- that's how they ended up at my place and that's where they died, and there can be no politics about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This civilian reclusive convoy, was it moving through your hamlet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: No, no. They were heading through Padjene.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And where was the convoy going, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, through Serb, then on to Drvar, and then further on through Strlija [phoen] Petrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were there also soldiers of the Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina travelling in that convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Of course, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you know if there were tanks of the Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina travelling in that convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: That I don't know. That I really don't know, because the road that leads through Padjene was three kilometres away, and there were two ends to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask the parties, whenever this is an question about the presence of soldiers, always to explore whether this was organised presence or whether it was one soldier not on duty among civilians, or together with other soldiers not from their own units, et cetera. That would certainly assist the Chamber in better understanding some of the issues at stake in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 69 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, no, there was no organisation there whatsoever. People were just fleeing any which way they could. That was the only thing to do. When you heard the thunder, everyone was just afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe what the Judge was asking you, with respect to the army being part of this convoy, was the army leaving in an organised manner as part of this convoy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That certainly was not what I intended to ask the witness. You earlier said that, of course, there were soldiers in the convoy. Could you tell us were these soldiers as part of a military unit, or were these soldiers just as individuals fleeing for their safety, or what were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those were individuals, individuals who just happened to be there, and they were just fleeing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And were they with other soldiers from their units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, definitely not. It was every man for himself. Everybody as going wherever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you tell us how you observed that there were soldiers? Did you see them or did you ask about the presence of soldiers in the convoy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I couldn't see them. They were three kilometres away, but everybody was trying to flee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are assuming that there must have been individual soldiers among those who were in the convoy. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. Some remained; some got killed, various fates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I need to go into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, just to inform you that we ended our last session in private session. I should have gone into open session when we discussed with the witness how much time we would need for the break. We are now in open session, again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 69, in your statement, you say that a Croatian soldier was forcing Dmitar to go with him. Was the Croatian --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was the Croatian soldier asking -- was the Croatian soldier asking Dmitar to show him directions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I wouldn't know that. That was around the corner. I couldn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You also indicate that when - let me just make sure - when the Croatian soldier took Dmitar behind his house, you heard a burst of automatic fire. I know it's difficult, 13 years later, but can you give us an approximation of how many rounds "a burst" is? Let me rephrase the question. How many rounds was the burst on the day that you heard it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, who could answer that, who could possibly know that, or who could possibly remember? It's been 13 years. I mean, how could you count them one by one? There was shooting all around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You said: "There was shooting all around." When you refer to this burst of automatic fire, were you saying that this burst came from the soldier who took Dmitar behind the house, or that you just heard gun-fire generally in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Gun-fire. Of course, I couldn't even see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, you said that later that afternoon, you went up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, let's try to clarify the issue. Witness 69, we do understand that you didn't see the gun-fire. Now, the burst of automatic fire, was that immediately after the Croatian soldier took Dmitar behind the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was right away; but whether the shooting was at him or at somebody else, what do I know? I didn't see it with my own eyes. I could only hear, and I was running.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you hear it shortly after the Croatian soldier had left with Dmitar behind the house, or was it within 30 seconds, or was it within five minutes, or was within 30 minutes, half an hour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A minute later, half a minute later, very quickly. Whether he was shooting at him or next to him, what do I know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what you heard, would the sound you heard, would that be compatible with a short distance, similar to Dmitar and the Croatian soldier behind the house, or was it from farther away? What came into your mind that you heard it, that it was from that location or from any other location, even if you did not see it, but from what you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think from a distance, but who could possibly judge that? It's like it was half a kilometre away, when, in fact, it was 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say: "In fact, it was 50 metres," but you did not see it. When you heard it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I didn't see it. I cannot tell you what did not happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But when you heard it, did it come into your mind that the burst of fire came approximately from where the two had left behind the house, or did it come into your mind that it came from another location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, nothing came to my mind except run, my legs, run. I don't think I was thinking at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just for the court's notification, I don't think it's appropriate with this witness, but I believe the Prosecution and/or the Defence will tender the autopsy report here, which may be relevant to this issue because there is one gunshot wound here, and we will discuss it later about the burst of gun-fire versus the one entry wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's correct. We were not planning on introducing these autopsy reports through this witness, but at some point we will lead it through a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But would it not be helpful for the Chamber to receive such an autopsy report as soon as possible whenever a witness testifies about such an event, so that we can see to what extent there is -- whether this report is compatible or incompatible with what the witness testifies? I mean, why wait?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's noted for the future cases when we will have a witness about killings, and we will try to get those document to the Chamber as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We don't have to be fed it perhaps in a similar way as a jury is fed with some pieces of information. We'll try to consider all the evidence as much as possible in the context. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness 69, you say in your statement that you ran 500 to 1.000 metres up the hill. From that position, you did not actually see how the fire at Djurdjija's house started, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: How could I possible see? I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And while you were in the forest, you encountered other people who were hiding in that forest as well, is that correct, without mentioning their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: That's when I went further away. It was not on the same day. I ran into those people 30 hours or 13 hours --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreter is not clear what the witness meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: May we go into private session, again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 69, we need to clarify one thing in the transcript, so I'm going to ask to you repeat it again. In one of your answers, I asked -- in one of my questions, I asked you whether you encountered other people who were hiding in that forest as well. You answered: "That's when I went further away. It was not on the same day. I ran into those people" 30 hours or 13 hours? Can you clarify what your answer was? Is it 30 hours later or 134 hours later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Thirty hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, in your statement, you say that you returned from the forest to your home on the 11th or 12th of August, and you noticed that your house was in disorder. Is it fair to say that your house, on that date, had been searched but had not been looted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: It wasn't looted. There was some pictures shattered, all sorts of objects and goods thrown in a heap.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And it wasn't until around the 15th of August that you started seeing people looting your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you were asked --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You were asked some questions earlier about who these people were. When these people arrived your hamlet, did they arrive in civilian cars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, they came in civilian cars. All of them were neighbours. Anyone can put on a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, you indicated, I believe in your testimony earlier, you said these were your neighbours who were coming from Zadar. Is that correct? Am I correctly characterising your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, from Zadar, from Split, from Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: These people, when they would loot in your hamlet, would they take the things back to Zadar and Split and Sibenik, or were they moving back into the area and keeping these things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: For the most part, it was taken further away and hidden in houses. I couldn't go to Zadar and see for myself the barrels and all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At some point in time, in late August, you arrived at the UN camp in Knin. Do you recall telling members of UN CIVPOL about the body that you had discovered of Ilija in your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: I explained it to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could call up 65 ter 4251. The witness will not have a copy of this in Zagreb, Mr. Registrar. If necessary, we will tender it from the bar table, but this is the UN CIVPOL report from September that encompasses this incident. For the record, Your Honour, again, we ask that this be marked and tendered into evidence from the bar table. It is a report from UN CIVPOL, sector chief, Jan Elleby, to the chief of policija, which is the MUP, Mr. Cetina, in Zadar, dated 19 September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Elleby will testify, so there is no objections to that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Maybe if I this would could be admitted under seal, as it has the names of some of the victims, so just that it is not linked with that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D179, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 69, I was remiss in not asking you one additional question. This looting that you saw, did you report it either to UN CIVPOL or to the Croatian police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: No way. To whom could I possibly report it? It was only later when I went to the UNPROFOR. Who was I supposed to report to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At some point, while you were in the UN camp, a Dr. Lang came to the camp as an emissary of President Tudjman. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what Dr. Lang said to the civilian population that was in the UN camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: He was talking nicely. He said those who will stay can stay and those who don't want to don't have to. But you know what people are like. People were afraid. They were afraid of getting killed. There was also the bishop from Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what the bishop from Sibenik said to the people in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, there were a lot of people there, a crowd. Some people asked for the floor and they allowed them to speak, and the people asked, "Are we all equal before God?" He couldn't answer that, except to say, "Yes." But why, then, would one person wants to kill another? That's the way it was. That's how it was, my brother. Who can remember all the details? It's all gone into oblivion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You, nevertheless, decided to leave Croatia in September 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: That's correct. For a family reunion, because everyone was gone. Some people were killed, some people came to a bad end. I don't know. I don't know how I was supposed to stay alone. It would have been very, very inconvenient.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: May we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is an disruption in the videolink. For this reason, we'll have a very short break and we'll continue immediately after the videolink has been restored, and then to finish without another break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the videolink has been restored, could I check with you, Mr. Registrar at the location of the videolink, whether you can see, whether you can hear us. Yes. Then it's up to you, Mr. Hedaraly, to put further questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I just have one point of clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Witness, this is about a response to a question put to you by Mr. Misetic, at transcript page 43, line 12 through 15. The question put to you was: "With respect to the army barracks at Padjene, do you know if any soldiers of the Republika Srpska Krajina evacuated from that location on the 5th of August? Then you answered: "Yes, they did." My only point of clarification for you is: Did you know that that was the date at which those soldiers had evacuated, or did you just know that they had evacuated in general?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, they left immediately on the 5th. By that time, they were all gone from Padjene.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You just said they were all gone by the 5th. So did they leave on the 5th, or before, or do you have any information as to when they left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It was -- it all happened during that night; and on the 5th, they were all gone. Well, nobody stayed; only the locals. But most of them were -- were gone. Only those who were infirm, who were old, they remained. I was called by them to go, too; but I didn't want to go. They were asking me, "Come with us." There was even a car, but why should I go, where should I go?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And who was telling you to go with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, neighbours. They tried to convince me that I should go and so did my wife. But I said, Where should I go? Why I would leave my home? Why would I leave my house? But at one point, the time came where I really had to go, or I had to leave it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 69, I have a few questions for you. You told us earlier that the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina soldiers were preparing for leaving. You said it was three or four days before the shelling happened. They were making their preparations, you said. Then you said: "They were pulling out heavy weapons already." Could you tell us where these heavy weapons were stationed that were pulled out, if you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know where it was put, where it was stored. All I know is that it left. It left in a space of two days in this general ruckus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now were there any heavy weapons in your hamlet.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: No, not at my place. There were no woods there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, there may be some confusion or misunderstanding. I asked you whether there were any heavy weapons, heavy weaponry in your hamlet just before the shelling started.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: About half a day before and up to half the night, there were some trucks up there in the woods between the two mountains. That's where they were, in those woods, and then they left. But two or three trucks remained there because there were not enough drivers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And these were trucks belonging to the Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, that was at what distance approximately from your hamlet? How much time would it take to you walk to where they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: There's one kilometre, less than a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say "less than a kilometre," could it be half a kilometre or close to a kilometre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, I didn't measure it. I didn't measure it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I asked you about your hamlet. What about your village, were you aware of any heavy weaponry in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: No, no. There were no weapons, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I move to another subject. You told us about the house of your neighbour Djurdjija that was burning, and you said: "I saw that her house suddenly went up in flame, together with hayloft." Now, could you tell us, this hayloft - I take it that is the same as a haystack, but I'm not a native English speaker - now what was the distance between the house and the haystack that burned? Could you tell us was it five metres from the house, was it 50 metres from the house? What is the distance between the haystack and the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: About 300 metres from my house. That's a house that is right by the side of the road. It's a detached house. Yes, right there by the side of the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you answer the question about the distance or at least your answer is about the distance between your house and the house of your neighbour. What I would like to know specifically was what was the distance? How many metres was the haystack from the house of your neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger just draw my attention that a hayloft apparently is the place with where the hay is stored, to be a separate structure, not just the haystack, for example, outside. Just to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at least that's good to know. I was in some doubt whether I understood the English sufficiently. Let's not confuse the witness. Now, in your statement you say that: "The house went up in flame, together with hayloft." Now was there a distance between the house and where the hay was stored?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Between the hay and the house, that's about ten metres. Well, you know how you store hay and what houses used for residential purposes look like, and both were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did they start burning at the same time, or was there a time interval; that is to say, that one started burning after three, four, or five minutes, or did they start burning at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, it's the same time. There is no difference. I'm looking from a vantage point. It's about 500 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you saw the house and the hayloft in flames, starting to be in flames at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have no further questions for you. Have the questions of the Bench triggered any need to put further questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, if I can just full up with a few question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Witness 69, a few more questions to you by Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 69, early in your testimony at page 16, lines 9 through 13, you said: "I don't know how many shells hit our area, but I can tell you that the lower part of the village that is on the other side of the railway track, that is where most of the shells fell. I take it from this answer, first, let me establish that there is a railway that divides your village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How far is your house from that railway track?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One further question for you, then, Witness 69, and it most likely will be the last one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you said that you do not know how many shells hit your area, but the lower part of the village, on the other side of the railway track, that is where most of the shells fell, what would we find there, the lower, other side of the railway track? Was it AN industrial area? Could you tell us what was hit by those shells on the lower part of the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: No, no. There's no barracks, there are no depots, nothing. It's just a village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you mean by "just a village," there were people living in their houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Of course. They lived there, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: But nobody got killed. Most of them fled. But even those that remained there, they were not killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There were no industrial complexes in that part of the village?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: (redacted) tanks; but it didn't catch fire or anything. The army had it, but they left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say that the storage of fuel and oil was an army storage of fuel an oil; although, the army had left. Is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Those were large tanks, large tanks holding fuel. I don't know what kind of fuel. Aeroplane fuel, I don't know. All of it was empty, there was nothing there, the buildings are being torn down. Everything is just being destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said the army had it. Could you tell me how did you know that these tanks, this storage of fuel and oil, was army fuel and oil?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-069
utterances.text: Well, the army had it, and a neighbour of mine worked on -- worked the engine that shunted those cars. That was just a few kilometres away from where I was, so how could I not know it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Again, last questions by the Bench triggered any need.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 69, this concludes your testimony. I would like to thank you very much for coming and for answering the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench. I hope that you'll be back home in time and that it did not, was not too much a burden for you to come to the place of the videolink. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the videolink is not needed anymore. Thank you very much at the other side of the line, Mr. Registrar, for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We now conclude the videolink, and we'll move on in The Hague. I'd like to turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, in this same courtroom, number II.
